UNH.rationale: UNH presents a mixed but slightly positive fundamental picture. Q1 2026 results showed a solid earnings beat ($7.23 adjusted EPS vs $6.57 expected) with revenue up 2% YoY to $111.7B and an improved medical loss ratio of 83.9% (down from 84.8%). Operating cash flow was strong at $8.9B (1.4x net income). However, the trajectory is complicated: the company is deliberately shedding ~1.3M Medicare Advantage members to protect margins, Optum revenue was flat-to-down, and net income was essentially flat YoY ($6.48B vs $6.47B). The balance sheet is sound with $103.9B equity and debt-to-capital improving to 42.9% toward a 40% target. On valuation, the stock has surged +31.9% in the last quarter to $382.48, pushing the P/E to 27.2x — the highest in the 12-month window (range 9.5-28.5) and well above the ~12-16x range that prevailed for most of the past year. P/B at 3.35x is also near the top of its 2.2-3.5 range. This means the market has already priced in much of the turnaround narrative. The raised FY2026 guidance to >$18.25 EPS provides some support, but at 27x that implies ~21x forward — no longer cheap. Berkshire Hathaway's full exit of its 5M share position is a negative sentiment signal, though not a fundamental catalyst. The 2027 Medicare Advantage payment rate increase of 2.48% (vs 0.09% proposed) is a genuine tailwind, but it's a 2027 story. Near-term catalysts are limited — the Q1 beat is already priced in, and the next earnings event is months away. Regulatory risks (DOJ investigations, PBM reform) and medical cost inflation from GLP-1 drugs remain meaningful headwinds. Net: decent franchise with improving execution, but valuation has run well ahead of the fundamental improvement, leaving a mildly positive but not compelling risk-reward.
